subject.title: fix: harden cloud worker admission and remote turns

question: Has Crabbox v0.38.1 or newer been published and verified through every supported install channel, and should OpenClaw now accept the intentional fail-closed upgrade boundary for existing AWS cloud workers?
rationale: The code depends on a newly landed provider-owned attestation contract, while deciding distribution readiness and accepting operator-visible upgrade impact require release-owner intent rather than another mechanical code change.

options.title: Publish, verify, then merge
options.body: Release Crabbox v0.38.1+, verify supported installation paths and live AWS admission, refresh the branch, and merge the fail-closed hardening.

options.title: Continue holding the PR
options.body: Keep the reviewed implementation open without merging until the dependency rollout and refreshed current-main proof are complete.

options.title: Preserve temporary compatibility
options.body: Revise the rollout to retain older Crabbox behavior temporarily, accepting a weaker admission boundary and requiring an explicit removal plan.

recommendation.title: Publish, verify, then merge
recommendation.body: Release Crabbox v0.38.1+, verify supported installation paths and live AWS admission, refresh the branch, and merge the fail-closed hardening.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history shows direct ownership of the cloud-worker design, OpenClaw implementation, companion Crabbox contract, and release coordination.
